Description: Cardinal Giuliano della Rovere is elected Pope and takes the name Julius II. [5]
The ceiling of the Sistine Chapel, painted by Michelangelo, is exhibited to the public for the first time.

The Strait of Magellan, the passage immediately south of mainland South America connecting the Pacific and the Atlantic Oceans, is first discovered and navigated by European explorer Ferdinand Magellan during the first recorded circumnavigation voyage.
Event title: European navigation of the Strait of Magellan

Description: The All Saints' Flood devastates the Dutch coast.
In Portugal, Lisbon is totally devastated by a massive earthquake and tsunami, killing an estimated 40,000 to 60,000 people.
The British Parliament enacts the Stamp Act on the Thirteen Colonies in order to help pay for British military operations in North America.
Congress of Vienna opens to re-draw the European political map after the defeat of France in the Napoleonic Wars.
In Boston, Massachusetts, the first medical school for women, Boston Female Medical School (which later merged with the Boston University School of Medicine), opens.
American Civil War: U.S. President Abraham Lincoln appoints George B. McClellan as the commander of the Union Army, replacing General Winfield Scott.
People involved: Abraham Lincoln; George B. McClellan; Winfield Scott

Description: In the United States, the Weather Bureau (later renamed the National Weather Service) makes its first official meteorological forecast.
Nicholas II becomes the new (and last) Tsar of Russia after his father, Alexander III, dies.
World's first combat aerial bombing mission takes place in Libya during the Italo-Turkish War. Second Lieutenant Giulio Gavotti of Italy drops several small bombs.

World War I: The first British Royal Navy defeat of the war with Germany, the Battle of Coronel, is fought off of the western coast of Chile, in the Pacific, with the loss of HMS Good Hope and HMS Monmouth.
Western Ukraine separates from Austria-Hungary.
Abolition of the Ottoman sultanate: The last sultan of the Ottoman Empire, Mehmed VI, abdicates.
Historical entity: Grand National Assembly of Turkey; Ottoman Empire

Description: The Law on the Adoption and Implementation of the Turkish Alphabet, replaces the Arabic alphabet with the Latin alphabet.

World War II: The 3rd Marine Division, United States Marines, landing on Bougainville in the Solomon Islands, secures a beachhead, leading that night to a naval clash at the Battle of Empress Augusta Bay.
Nuclear weapons testing: The United States successfully detonates Ivy Mike, the first thermonuclear device, at the Eniwetok atoll. The explosion had a yield of ten megatons TNT equivalent. [11]
The Front de Libération Nationale fires the first shots of the Algerian War of Independence.
The Maastricht Treaty takes effect, formally establishing the European Union. [15]
The French Directory, a five-man revolutionary government, is created. [5]
North Dakota and South Dakota are admitted as the 39th and 40th U.S. states. [8]
Event title: North Dakota and South Dakota admitted to the United States

Description: World War I: The Russian Empire declares war on the Ottoman Empire and the Dardanelles is subsequently closed. [11]
Event title: Russia declared war on the Ottoman Empire

Description: The Balfour Declaration proclaims British support for the "establishment in Palestine of a national home for the Jewish people" with the clear understanding "that nothing shall be done which may prejudice the civil and religious rights of existing non-Jewish communities". [12]
In the United States, KDKA of Pittsburgh starts broadcasting as the first commercial radio station. The first broadcast is the result of the 1920 United States presidential election. [15]
The BBC Television Service, the world's first regular, "high-definition" (then defined as at least 200 lines) service begins. Renamed BBC1 in 1964, the channel still runs to this day. [16]
The Dutch–Indonesian Round Table Conference ends with the Netherlands agreeing to transfer sovereignty of the Dutch East Indies to the United States of Indonesia. [19]
Suez Crisis: Israel occupies the Gaza Strip. [22]
Quiz show scandals: Twenty-One game show contestant Charles Van Doren admits to a Congressional committee that he had been given questions and answers in advance. [23]
Event title: Charles Van Doren admitted quiz-show deception

Description: Penguin Books is found not guilty of obscenity in the trial R v Penguin Books Ltd, the Lady Chatterley's Lover case. [25]
South Vietnamese President Ngô Đình Diệm is assassinated following a military coup. [26]
King Saud of Saudi Arabia is deposed by a family coup, and replaced by his half-brother Faisal. [27]
The Cuban Adjustment Act comes into force, allowing 123,000 Cubans the opportunity to apply for permanent residence in the United States. [29]
U.S. President Ronald Reagan signs a bill creating Martin Luther King Jr. Day. [33]
Event title: Martin Luther King Jr. Day created
People involved: Ronald Reagan; Martin Luther King Jr.

Description: The Morris worm, the first Internet-distributed computer worm to gain significant mainstream media attention, is launched from MIT. [36]
Tropical Storm Linda makes landfall in the Mekong Delta in Vietnam, causing more than 3,000 deaths. [39]

Expedition 1 arrived at the International Space Station for the first long-duration stay onboard. From this day to present, a continuous human presence in space on the station remains uninterrupted. [41] [42]
Event title: Expedition 1 arrived at the International Space Station

Description: Christopher Columbus first sights the island of Dominica in the Caribbean Sea.
English Parliament passes the first Act of Supremacy, making King Henry VIII head of the Anglican Church, supplanting the pope and the Roman Catholic Church.
The American Continental Army is disbanded.
French playwright, journalist and feminist Olympe de Gouges is guillotined.
Napoleon's armies are defeated at the Battle of Vyazma.
A greatly revised Dutch constitution, which transfers much authority from the king to his parliament and ministers, is proclaimed.
Giuseppe Garibaldi and his followers are defeated in the Battle of Mentana and fail to end the Pope's Temporal power in Rome (it would be achieved three years later).
John Willis Menard (R-LA) becomes the first African American elected to the United States Congress. Because of an electoral challenge, he is never seated.
Event title: John Willis Menard elected to Congress

Description: France withdraws its troops from Fashoda (now in Sudan), ending the Fashoda Incident.
With the encouragement of the United States, Panama separates from Colombia.
Historical entity: Republic of Panama; Republic of Colombia

Description: The German Revolution of 1918–19 begins when 40,000 sailors take over the port in Kiel.
Franklin D. Roosevelt is reelected as President of the United States.
The Constitution of Japan is adopted through Emperor's assent.
Air India Flight 245 crashes into Mont Blanc while on approach to Geneva Airport, killing all 48 people on board. [4]
Sputnik program: The Soviet Union launches Sputnik 2. [5] On board is the first animal to enter orbit, a dog named Laika. [6]
U Thant is unanimously appointed as the 3rd Secretary-General of the United Nations, becoming the first non-European individual to occupy the post. [7]

Lyndon B. Johnson is elected to a full term as U.S. president, winning 61% of the vote and 44 states, while Washington D.C. residents are able to vote in a presidential election for the first time, casting the majority of their votes for Lyndon Johnson.
Mariner program: NASA launches the Mariner 10 toward Mercury. [9] On March 29, 1974, it becomes the first space probe to reach that planet. [10]
Dominica gains its independence from the United Kingdom.

Iran–Contra affair: The Lebanese magazine Ash-Shiraa reports that the United States has been secretly selling weapons to Iran in order to secure the release of seven American hostages held by pro-Iranian groups in Lebanon.
Eighty Years' War: In Flanders, Spain captures Antwerp (which is nearly destroyed after three days).
The Rebellion of Túpac Amaru II against Spanish rule in the Viceroyalty of Peru begins.
Northwest Indian War: The Western Confederacy of American Indians wins a major victory over the United States in the Battle of the Wabash.
Newport Rising: The last large-scale armed rebellion against authority in mainland Britain.
Sir James Young Simpson, a Scottish medical doctor, discovers the anaesthetic properties of chloroform.
Camillo Benso, Count of Cavour, becomes the prime minister of Piedmont- Sardinia, which soon expands to become Italy.
Event title: Cavour becomes prime minister of Piedmont-Sardinia

Description: City and South London Railway: London's first deep-level tube railway opens between King William Street and Stockwell.
Event title: London's first deep-level tube railway opens

Description: World War I: The Armistice of Villa Giusti between Italy and Austria-Hungary is implemented.
Japanese prime minister Hara Takashi is assassinated in Tokyo.
In Egypt, British archaeologist Howard Carter and his men find the entrance to Tutankhamun's tomb in the Valley of the Kings.
Nellie Tayloe Ross of Wyoming becomes the first female elected as governor in the United States.
World War II: U.S. president Franklin D. Roosevelt orders the United States Customs Service to implement the Neutrality Act of 1939, allowing cash-and-carry purchases of weapons by belligerents.
Event title: United States implements cash-and-carry neutrality policy

Description: The United States government establishes the National Security Agency, or NSA.

Soviet troops enter Hungary to end the Hungarian revolution against the Soviet Union that started on October 23. Thousands are killed, more are wounded, and nearly a quarter million leave the country.
At the Kasakela Chimpanzee Community in Tanzania, Jane Goodall observes chimpanzees creating tools, the first-ever observation in non-human animals.

The Arno River floods Florence, Italy, to a maximum depth of 6.7 m (22 ft), leaving thousands homeless and destroying millions of masterpieces of art and rare books. Venice is also submerged on the same day at its record all-time acqua alta of 194 cm (76 in).
Salvador Allende takes office as President of Chile, the first Marxist to become president of a Latin American country through open elections.
Iran hostage crisis: A group of Iranian college students overruns the U.S. embassy in Tehran and takes 90 hostages.
Historical entity: Islamic Student Followers of the Imam's Line; United States embassy

Description: Israel-Palestinian conflict: Israeli prime minister Yitzhak Rabin is assassinated by an extremist Israeli.
Barack Obama becomes the first person of biracial or African-American descent to be elected as President of the United States.
Gunpowder Plot: Guy Fawkes is arrested in the cellars of the Houses of Parliament, where he had planted gunpowder in an attempt to blow up the building and kill King James I of England. [2]
Event title: Guy Fawkes arrested in the Gunpowder Plot

Description: Seven Years' War: Frederick the Great defeats the allied armies of France and the Holy Roman Empire at the Battle of Rossbach.
Salvadoran priest José Matías Delgado rings the bells of La Merced church in San Salvador, calling for insurrection and launching the 1811 Independence Movement.
American Civil War: Abraham Lincoln removes George B. McClellan as commander of the Army of the Potomac.
Women's suffrage in the United States: In defiance of the law, suffragist Susan B. Anthony votes for the first time, and is later fined $100.

In New Zealand, 1600 armed volunteers and constabulary field forces led by Minister of Native Affairs John Bryce march on the pacifist Māori settlement at Parihaka, evicting upwards of 2000 residents, and destroying the settlement in the context of the New Zealand land confiscations. [5]
George B. Selden is granted the first U.S. patent for an automobile.
Woodrow Wilson is elected the 28th President of the United States, defeating incumbent William Howard Taft.
World War I: France and the British Empire declare war on the Ottoman Empire.
Event title: Britain and France declare war on the Ottoman Empire

Description: The Kingdom of Poland is proclaimed by the Act of 5th November of the emperors of Germany and Austria-Hungary.
Historical entity: Kingdom of Poland; German Empire; Austria-Hungary

Description: Tikhon is elected the Patriarch of Moscow and of the Russian Orthodox Church.
Franklin D. Roosevelt is the first and only President of the United States to be elected to a third term.
Event title: Franklin D. Roosevelt wins a third presidential term

Description: Suez Crisis: British and French paratroopers land in Egypt after a week-long bombing campaign.
Event title: British and French forces land in Egypt

Description: Richard Nixon is elected as 37th President of the United States.
The Byford Dolphin diving bell accident kills five and leaves one severely injured.
Tropical Storm Thelma causes flash floods in the Philippine city of Ormoc, killing more than 4,900 people. [7]
Pakistani President Farooq Leghari dismisses the government of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto and dissolves the National Assembly.
Bill Clinton is reelected President of the United States.

Saddam Hussein, the former president of Iraq, and his co-defendants Barzan Ibrahim al-Tikriti and Awad Hamed al-Bandar, are sentenced to death in the al-Dujail trial for their roles in the 1982 massacre of 148 Shia Muslims.
People involved: Saddam Hussein; Barzan Ibrahim al-Tikriti; Awad Hamed al-Bandar

Description: China's first lunar satellite, Chang'e 1, goes into orbit around the Moon.
A powerful earthquake destroys large portions of the Walls of Constantinople, including 57 towers. [1]

The Charter of the Forest is sealed at St Paul's Cathedral, London by King Henry III, acting under the regency of William Marshall, 1st Earl of Pembroke which re-establishes for free men rights of access to the royal forest that had been eroded by William the Conqueror and his heirs. [3]
Battle of Jemappes in the French Revolutionary Wars. [4]
Abraham Lincoln is elected the 16th president of the United States with only 40% of the popular vote, defeating John C. Breckinridge, John Bell, and Stephen A. Douglas in a four-way race. [5]
People involved: Abraham Lincoln; John C. Breckinridge; John Bell; Stephen A. Douglas

Description: President William McKinley is re-elected, along with his vice-presidential running mate, Governor Theodore Roosevelt of New York. [7]
Spanish Civil War: The republican government flees from Madrid to Valencia, leading to the formation of the Madrid Defense Council in its stead. [8]
World War II: The 1st Ukrainian Front liberates Kyiv from German occupation. [9]
Nguyễn Ngọc Thơ is appointed to head the South Vietnamese government by General Dương Văn Minh's junta, five days after the latter deposed and assassinated President Ngô Đình Diệm. [11]
Event title: Nguyễn Ngọc Thơ heads South Vietnamese government
People involved: Nguyễn Ngọc Thơ; Dương Văn Minh; Ngô Đình Diệm

Description: The United States Atomic Energy Commission tests the largest U.S. underground hydrogen bomb, code-named Cannikin, on Amchitka Island in the Aleutians. [12]
Uttawar forced sterilisations: Mass vasectomy of nearly 800 men of Uttawar village, Palwal district, Haryana during India's Emergency imposed by Indira Gandhi. [13]
The Kelly Barnes Dam, located above Toccoa Falls College near Toccoa, Georgia, fails, killing 39. [14]
Colombian conflict: leftist guerrillas of the 19th of April Movement seize control of the Palace of Justice in Bogotá. [15]

Sumburgh disaster: A British International Helicopters Boeing 234LR Chinook crashes 2.5 miles (4.0 km) east of Sumburgh Airport killing 45 people. It is the deadliest civilian helicopter crash on record. [16]
Lancang–Gengma earthquakes: At least 730 are killed after two powerful earthquakes rock the China–Myanmar border in Yunnan Province. [17]
The Sixth Ecumenical Council commences in Constantinople.
Lam Sơn uprising: Lam Sơn rebels emerge victorious against the Ming army in the Battle of Tốt Động – Chúc Động taking place in Đông Quan, in now Hanoi.
The Ensisheim meteorite, the oldest meteorite with a known date of impact, strikes the Earth in a wheat field outside the village of Ensisheim, Alsace, France.

John Murray (also known as Lord Dunmore), the Royal Governor of the Colony of Virginia, starts the first mass emancipation of slaves in North America by issuing Lord Dunmore's Offer of Emancipation, which offers freedom to slaves who abandoned their colonial masters to fight with Murray and the British.
Tecumseh's War: The Battle of Tippecanoe is fought near present-day Battle Ground, Indiana, United States.
In Alton, Illinois, abolitionist printer Elijah P. Lovejoy is shot dead by a mob while attempting to protect his printing shop from being destroyed a third time.
The completion of Canada's first transcontinental railway is symbolized by the Last Spike ceremony at Craigellachie, British Columbia.
Women's suffrage: Women in the U.S. state of Colorado are granted the right to vote, the second state to do so.
The German colony of Kiaochow Bay and its centre at Tsingtao are captured by Japanese forces. This leaves Germany without a far east base.
Jeannette Rankin is the first woman elected to the United States Congress.

Notes: The October Revolution is dated 25 October in the Julian calendar.
Description: The October Revolution, which gets its name from the Julian calendar date of 25 October, occurs, according to the Gregorian calendar; on this date, the Bolsheviks storm the Winter Palace.
Original date: The October Revolution is dated 25 October in the Julian calendar.

Description: World War I: The Third Battle of Gaza ends, with British forces capturing Gaza from the Ottoman Empire.
Kurt Eisner overthrows the Wittelsbach dynasty in the Kingdom of Bavaria.
The first Palmer Raid is conducted on the second anniversary of the Russian Revolution. Over 10,000 suspected communists and anarchists are arrested in 23 U.S. cities.
In New York City, the Museum of Modern Art opens to the public.
In Tacoma, Washington, the original Tacoma Narrows Bridge collapses in a windstorm, a mere four months after the bridge's completion.
Suez Crisis: The United Nations General Assembly adopts a resolution calling for the United Kingdom, France and Israel to immediately withdraw their troops from Egypt.
Event title: UN calls for withdrawal during Suez Crisis

Description: Carl B. Stokes is elected as Mayor of Cleveland, Ohio, becoming the first African American mayor of a major American city.
Event title: Carl Stokes elected mayor of Cleveland

Description: The United States Congress overrides President Richard Nixon's veto of the War Powers Resolution, which limits presidential power to wage war without congressional approval.
In Tunisia, president Habib Bourguiba is overthrown and replaced by Prime Minister Zine El Abidine Ben Ali.
People involved: Habib Bourguiba; Zine El Abidine Ben Ali

Description: Hernán Cortés enters Tenochtitlán and Aztec ruler Moctezuma welcomes him with a great celebration.
Eighty Years' War: Pacification of Ghent: The States General of the Netherlands meet and unite to oppose Spanish occupation.
Historical entity: States General of the Netherlands; Spanish Empire

Description: The Battle of White Mountain takes place near Prague, ending in a decisive Catholic victory in only two hours.
The Shunzhi Emperor, the third emperor of the Qing dynasty, is enthroned in Beijing after the collapse of the Ming dynasty as the first Qing emperor to rule over China.
Mary Lyon founds Mount Holyoke Female Seminary, which later becomes Mount Holyoke College.
Event title: Founding of Mount Holyoke Female Seminary

Description: American Civil War: The " Trent Affair": The USS San Jacinto stops the British mail ship Trent and arrests two Confederate envoys, sparking a diplomatic crisis between the UK and US.
Historical entity: United States Navy; Confederate States of America

Description: Montana is admitted as the 41st U.S. state.
The New Orleans general strike begins, uniting black and white American trade unionists in a successful four-day general strike action for the first time.
While experimenting with electricity, Wilhelm Röntgen discovers the X-ray.
The first Council of People's Commissars is formed, including Vladimir Lenin, Leon Trotsky and Joseph Stalin.
Event title: First Council of People's Commissars formed
People involved: Vladimir Lenin; Leon Trotsky; Joseph Stalin

Description: Beer Hall Putsch: In Munich, Adolf Hitler leads the Nazis in an unsuccessful attempt to overthrow the German government.
Franklin D. Roosevelt is elected as the 32nd President of the United States, defeating incumbent president Herbert Hoover.
In Munich, Adolf Hitler narrowly escapes the assassination attempt of Georg Elser while celebrating the 16th anniversary of the Beer Hall Putsch.

World War II: French Resistance coup in Algiers, in which 400 civilian French patriots neutralize Vichyist XIXth Army Corps after 15 hours of fighting, and arrest several Vichyist generals, allowing the immediate success of Operation Torch in Algiers.
Korean War: United States Air Force Lt. Russell J. Brown, while piloting an F-80 Shooting Star, shoots down two North Korean MiG-15s in the first jet aircraft-to-jet aircraft dogfight in history.
Historical entity: United States Air Force; Korean People's Army Air Force

Description: Operation Grapple X, Round C1: The United Kingdom conducts its first successful hydrogen bomb test over Kiritimati in the Pacific.
John F. Kennedy is elected as the 35th President of the United States, defeating incumbent Vice President Richard Nixon, who would later be elected president in 1968 and 1972.
The Murder (Abolition of Death Penalty) Act 1965 is given Royal Assent, formally abolishing the death penalty in the United Kingdom for almost all crimes.
Event title: United Kingdom abolishes most death penalties

Description: Remembrance Day bombing: A Provisional IRA bomb explodes in Enniskillen, Northern Ireland during a ceremony honouring those who had died in wars involving British forces. Twelve people are killed and sixty-three wounded.

Iraq disarmament crisis: UN Security Council Resolution 1441: The United Nations Security Council unanimously approves a resolution on Iraq, forcing Saddam Hussein to disarm or face "serious consequences".
At the Seventeenth Council of Toledo, Egica, a king of the Visigoths of Hispania, accuses Jews of aiding Muslims, sentencing all Jews to slavery.
Event title: Seventeenth Council of Toledo sanctions Jews

Description: The Battle of Fujigawa: Minamoto forces (30,000 men) under Minamoto no Yoritomo defeat Taira no Koremori during a night attack near the Fuji River but he escapes safely with the routed army. [1] [2]
People involved: Minamoto no Yoritomo; Taira no Koremori

Description: The Treaty of Aberconwy, a humiliating settlement forced on Llywelyn ap Gruffudd by King Edward I of England, brings a temporary end to the Welsh Wars. [3]
Historical entity: Kingdom of England; Principality of Wales

Description: More than 50 people are sentenced and executed in the Stockholm Bloodbath.
Second Desmond Rebellion: The Siege of Smerwick ends with the Catholic garrison surrendering to the English forces under Arthur Grey. The majority of the garrison is massacred the next day. [9] [10]
Napoleon Bonaparte leads the Coup of 18 Brumaire ending the Directory government, and becoming First Consul of the successor Consulate Government.
The Tokugawa shogunate hands back power to the Emperor of Japan, starting the Meiji Restoration.
Historical entity: Tokugawa shogunate; Imperial House of Japan

Description: The Great Boston Fire of 1872.
A major earthquake strikes Zagreb and destroys many buildings, including Zagreb Cathedral. [14] [15]
The United States receives rights to Pearl Harbor, Hawaii.
Event title: United States obtains Pearl Harbor rights

Description: The Great Lakes Storm of 1913, the most destructive natural disaster ever to hit the lakes, reaches its greatest intensity after beginning two days earlier. The storm destroys 19 ships and kills more than 250 people.
The Balfour Declaration is published in The Times newspaper. [22]
Kaiser Wilhelm II of Germany abdicates after the German Revolution, and Germany is proclaimed a Republic.
Kristallnacht occurs, instigated by the Nazis using the killing of German diplomat Ernst vom Rath by Herschel Grynszpan as justification.
An agreement for the founding of the United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration [28] is signed by 44 countries in the White House, Washington, D.C. [29]
Event title: United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration founded
Historical entity: United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration

Description: Cambodia gains independence from France.
At a coal mine in Miike, Japan, an explosion kills 458 and hospitalises 839 with carbon monoxide poisoning.
Several U.S. states and parts of Canada are hit by a series of blackouts lasting up to 13 hours in the Northeast blackout of 1965.
Apollo program: NASA launches the unmanned Apollo 4 test spacecraft, atop the first Saturn V rocket, from Florida's Cape Kennedy.

Cold War: Nuclear false alarm: The NORAD computers and the Alternate National Military Command Center in Fort Ritchie, Maryland, detect a purported massive Soviet nuclear strike. After reviewing the raw data from satellites and checking the early-warning radars, the alert is cancelled.
Historical entity: NORAD; Alternate National Military Command Center

Description: Battle of Varna: The crusading forces of King Władysław III of Poland (aka Ulaszlo I of Hungary and Władysław III of Varna) are defeated by the Turks under Sultan Murad II and Władysław is killed.
The United States Marine Corps is founded at Tun Tavern in Philadelphia by Samuel Nicholas.
A Goddess of Reason is proclaimed by the French Convention at the suggestion of Pierre Gaspard Chaumette.
Cry of Independence by Rufina Alfaro at La Villa de Los Santos, Panama setting into motion a revolt which led to Panama's independence from Spain and to it immediately becoming part of Colombia.
Event title: Cry of Independence at La Villa de Los Santos

Description: Henry Morton Stanley locates missing explorer and missionary, David Livingstone in Ujiji, near Lake Tanganyika, famously greeting him with the words, "Dr. Livingstone, I presume?" [3]
White supremacists seized power and massacred black Americans during the Wilmington massacre, the only instance of a municipal government being overthrown in United States history.
The 1940 Vrancea earthquake strikes Romania killing an estimated 1,000 and injuring approximately 4,000 more.
World War II: Germany invades Vichy France following French Admiral François Darlan's agreement to an armistice with the Allies in North Africa.
The ammunition ship USS Mount Hood explodes at Seeadler Harbour, Manus, Admiralty Islands, killing at least 432 and wounding 371.

Notes: Today celebrated in Indonesia as Heroes' Day (Hari Pahlawan).; (Hari Pahlawan)
Description: Heavy fighting in Surabaya between Indonesian nationalists and returning colonialists after World War II, today celebrated as Heroes' Day (Hari Pahlawan).
With the rollout of the North American Numbering Plan, direct-dial coast-to-coast telephone service begins in the United States.
The Nauru Independence Act 1967 passed the Parliament of Australia, giving independence to the UN Trust Territory of Nauru with effect from 31 January 1968. [6]
Historical entity: Parliament of Australia; United Nations Trust Territory of Nauru

Notes: National Educational Television was the predecessor to the Public Broadcasting Service.
Description: National Educational Television (the predecessor to the Public Broadcasting Service) in the United States debuts Sesame Street.
Luna 17: uncrewed space mission launched by the Soviet Union. [3]
The 729-foot-long freighter SS Edmund Fitzgerald sinks during a storm on Lake Superior, killing all 29 crew on board.
Israeli-Palestinian conflict: the United Nations General Assembly passes Resolution 3379, determining that Zionism is a form of racism. [9]
Bill Gates introduces Windows 1.0.
Longtime Bulgarian leader Todor Zhivkov is removed from office and replaced by Petar Mladenov.
Germans begin to tear down the Berlin Wall.
In Nigeria, playwright and environmental activist Ken Saro-Wiwa, along with eight others from the Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People (Mosop), are hanged by government forces.
Historical entity: Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People; Nigerian government

Description: The Fourth Council of the Lateran meets, defining the doctrine of transubstantiation, the process by which bread and wine are, by that doctrine, said to transform into the body and blood of Christ.
Event title: Fourth Council of the Lateran opens

Description: Tycho Brahe observes the supernova SN 1572.
The Mayflower Compact is signed in what is now Provincetown Harbor near Cape Cod.

Second Battle of Khotyn in Ukraine: Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth forces under the command of Jan Sobieski defeat the Ottoman army. In this battle, rockets made by Kazimierz Siemienowicz are successfully used.
Cherry Valley massacre: Loyalists and Seneca Indian forces attack a fort and village in eastern New York during the American Revolutionary War, killing more than forty civilians and soldiers.
Napoleonic Wars: Battle of Dürenstein: Eight thousand French troops attempt to slow the retreat of a vastly superior Russian and Austrian force.
Historical entity: French Empire; Russian Empire; Austrian Empire

Description: A powerful earthquake occurs in Edo, Japan, causing considerable damage in the Kantō region from the shaking and subsequent fires. It had a death toll of 7,000–10,000 people and destroyed around 14,000 buildings. [2]

The Victorian Aboriginal Protection Act is enacted in Australia, giving the government control of indigenous people's wages, their terms of employment, where they could live, and of their children, effectively leading to the Stolen Generations.
Four convicted anarchists were executed as a result of the Haymarket affair. [3]
The State of Washington is admitted as the 42nd state of the United States. [4]
World War I: Germany signs an armistice agreement with the Allies in a railroad car in the forest of Compiègne. [5]
Modern country: France; Germany; United Kingdom; United States; Belgium; Italy

Description: Józef Piłsudski assumes supreme military power in Poland – symbolic first day of Polish independence.
Adolf Hitler is arrested in Munich for high treason for his role in the Beer Hall Putsch.
Event title: Adolf Hitler arrested after Beer Hall Putsch

Description: World War II: In the Battle of Taranto, the Royal Navy launches the first all-aircraft ship-to-ship naval attack in history.
World War II: France's zone libre is occupied by German forces in Case Anton.

The Turkish parliament passes the Varlık Vergisi, [7] a capital tax mostly levied on non-Muslim citizens with the unofficial aim to inflict financial ruin on them and end their prominence in the country's economy. [8] [9] [10]
Southern Rhodesia's Prime Minister Ian Smith unilaterally declares the colony independent as the unrecognised state of Rhodesia.
NASA launches Gemini 12.

Australian constitutional crisis of 1975: Australian Governor-General Sir John Kerr dismisses the government of Gough Whitlam, appoints Malcolm Fraser as caretaker Prime Minister and announces a general election to be held in early December.
People involved: Sir John Kerr; Gough Whitlam; Malcolm Fraser

Description: Russian mathematician Grigori Perelman posts the first of three preprint texts with his proof of the Poincaré conjecture. It remains the only of the Millennium Prize Problems in mathematics to be solved. He later refused both the prize money from Clay Mathematics Institute as well as the Fields Medal for his work. [16]
Battle of Posada ends: Wallachian Voievode Basarab I defeats the Hungarian army by ambush. [3]
Historical entity: Principality of Wallachia; Kingdom of Hungary

Description: Abdur Rahman Khan accepts the Durand Line as the border between the Emirate of Afghanistan and the British Raj.
First Balkan War: King George I of Greece makes a triumphal entry into Thessaloniki after its liberation from 482 years of Ottoman rule.
The frozen bodies of Robert Scott and his men are found on the Ross Ice Shelf in Antarctica. [6]
Dissolution of Austria-Hungary: Austria becomes a republic. [7] After the proclamation, a coup attempt by the communist Red Guard is defeated by the social-democratic Volkswehr. [8]
Leon Trotsky is expelled from the Soviet Communist Party, leaving Joseph Stalin in undisputed control of the Soviet Union.
Event title: Trotsky expelled from Soviet Communist Party

Description: SS Vestris sinks approximately 200 miles (320 km) off Hampton Roads, Virginia, killing at least 110 passengers, mostly women and children who die after the vessel is abandoned.

Nazi Germany issues the Decree on the Elimination of Jews from Economic Life prohibiting Jews from selling goods and services or working in a trade, totally segregating Jews from the German economy. [12]
Event title: Nazi decree excluding Jews from the economy

Description: World War II: The Battle of Gabon ends as Free French Forces take Libreville, Gabon, and all of French Equatorial Africa from Vichy French forces.
World War II: Naval Battle of Guadalcanal between Japanese and American forces begins near Guadalcanal. The battle lasts for three days and ends with an American victory.
Historical entity: United States Navy; Imperial Japanese Navy

Description: World War II: The Royal Air Force sink the German battleship Tirpitz, moored off Tromsø, Norway. [14]

Aftermath of World War II: In Tokyo, the International Military Tribunal for the Far East sentences seven Japanese military and government officials, including General Hideki Tojo, to death for their roles in World War II.
Historical entity: International Military Tribunal for the Far East

Description: Ellis Island ceases operations. [15]
The 1970 Bhola cyclone makes landfall on the coast of East Pakistan, becoming the deadliest tropical cyclone in history.
The NASA space probe Voyager I makes its closest approach to Saturn and takes the first images of its rings.
Space Shuttle program: Mission STS-2, utilizing the Space Shuttle Columbia, marks the first time a crewed spacecraft is launched into space twice.
Crown Prince Akihito is formally installed as Emperor Akihito of Japan, becoming the 125th Japanese monarch.
Tim Berners-Lee publishes a formal proposal for the World Wide Web.
Santa Cruz massacre: The Indonesian Army open fire on a crowd of student protesters in Dili, East Timor.
The 7.2 M w Düzce earthquake shakes northwestern Turkey with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent). At least 845 people are killed and almost 5,000 are injured.
English king Æthelred II orders the killing of all Danes in England, known today as the St. Brice's Day massacre. [1]
American Revolutionary War: Patriot revolutionary forces under Gen. Richard Montgomery occupy Montreal.
Great Meteor Storm of 1833. [7]
The Denny Party lands at Alki Point, before moving to the other side of Elliott Bay to what would become Seattle.
Zaian War: Berber tribesmen inflict the heaviest defeat of French forces in Morocco at the Battle of El Herri.
World War I: Allied troops occupy Constantinople, the capital of the Ottoman Empire.
The United States Supreme Court upholds mandatory vaccinations for public school students in Zucht v. King. [13]
Historical entity: Supreme Court of the United States

Description: The Holland Tunnel opens to traffic as the first Hudson River vehicle tunnel linking New Jersey to New York City.
Historical entity: Port Authority of New York and New Jersey

Description: World War II: Naval Battle of Guadalcanal: U.S. and Japanese ships engage in an intense, close-quarters surface naval engagement during the Guadalcanal campaign. [14]
Historical entity: United States Navy; Imperial Japanese Navy

Description: The Supreme Court of the United States affirmed a lower court ruling that invalidated Alabama laws requiring segregated buses, thus ending the Montgomery bus boycott.
Historical entity: Supreme Court of the United States

Description: Vietnam War: Anti-war protesters in Washington, D.C. stage a symbolic March Against Death.
Bhola cyclone: A 240 km/h (150 mph) tropical cyclone hits the densely populated Ganges Delta region of East Pakistan (now Bangladesh), killing an estimated 500,000 people in one night.
The Vietnam Veterans Memorial is dedicated in Washington, D.C. after a march to its site by thousands of Vietnam War veterans.
The volcano Nevado del Ruiz erupts and melts a glacier, causing a lahar (volcanic mudslide) that buries Armero, Colombia, killing approximately 23,000 people.
In Aramoana, New Zealand, David Gray shoots dead 13 people in a massacre before being tracked down and killed by police the next day.
In a referendum, voters in Sweden decide to join the European Union.
Event title: Swedish referendum on European Union membership

Description: Mozambique becomes the first state to join the Commonwealth of Nations without having been part of the former British Empire. [21]

War on terror: In the first such act since World War II, US President George W. Bush signs an executive order allowing military tribunals against foreigners suspected of connections to terrorist acts or planned acts on the United States.
Iraq disarmament crisis: Iraq agrees to the terms of the UN Security Council Resolution 1441.
German astronomer Gottfried Kirch discovers the Great Comet of 1680, the first comet to be discovered by telescope. [2]
Event title: Discovery of the Great Comet of 1680

Description: Napoleonic Wars: At the Battle of Smoliani, French Marshals Victor and Oudinot are defeated by the Russians under General Peter Wittgenstein. [4]
Moby-Dick, a novel by Herman Melville, is published in the USA. [5]
Pioneering female journalist Nellie Bly (aka Elizabeth Cochrane) begins a successful attempt to travel around the world in less than 80 days. She completes the trip in 72 days. [6]
Aviator Eugene Burton Ely performs the first takeoff from a ship in Hampton Roads, Virginia, taking off from a makeshift deck on the USS Birmingham in a Curtiss pusher.
The Provisional National Assembly of the new republic of Czechoslovakia meets to devise a constitution. [8]
The British Broadcasting Company begins radio service in the United Kingdom. [11]
World War II: In England, Coventry is heavily bombed by German Luftwaffe bombers. Coventry Cathedral is almost completely destroyed.
World War II: The aircraft carrier HMS Ark Royal sinks due to torpedo damage from the German submarine U-81 sustained on November 13.
World War II: German troops, aided by local auxiliaries, murder nine thousand residents of the Słonim Ghetto in a single day.
The " Apalachin meeting" in rural Tioga County in upstate New York is raided by law enforcement; many high-level Mafia figures are arrested while trying to flee.
Ruby Bridges becomes the first black child to attend an all-white elementary school in Louisiana.
Event title: Ruby Bridges enters a formerly segregated school

Description: Vietnam War: The Battle of Ia Drang begins. This is the first major engagement between regular American and North Vietnamese forces.
Historical entity: United States Armed Forces; North Vietnamese forces

Description: American physicist Theodore Maiman is given a patent for his ruby laser systems, the world's first laser.
Apollo program: NASA launches Apollo 12, the second crewed mission to the surface of the Moon.
Mariner 9 enters orbit around Mars.
With the signing of the Madrid Accords, Spain abandons Western Sahara.
US President Jimmy Carter issues Executive Order 12170, freezing all Iranian assets in the United States in response to the hostage crisis.
Lech Wałęsa, the leader of Poland's outlawed Solidarity movement, is released after eleven months of internment near the Soviet border.
After German reunification, the Federal Republic of Germany and Poland sign a treaty confirming the Oder–Neisse line as the border between Germany and Poland.
Historical entity: Federal Republic of Germany; Republic of Poland

Description: American Revolutionary War: After 16 months of debate the Continental Congress approves the Articles of Confederation.
Event title: Continental Congress approves the Articles of Confederation

Description: American Civil War: Union General William Tecumseh Sherman begins his March to the Sea through Georgia towards the city of Savannah. [5]
Event title: Sherman’s March to the Sea begins

Description: The Berlin Conference of 1884–1885 met on 15 November 1884, and after an adjournment concluded on 26 February 1885, with the signature of a General Act, regulating the European colonisation and trade in Africa during the New Imperialism period. [6]
Brazil is declared a republic by Marshal Deodoro da Fonseca as Emperor Pedro II is deposed in a military coup.
Eduskunta declares itself the supreme state power of Finland, prompting its declaration of independence and secession from Russia. [8]
Event title: Finland’s parliament declares supreme state power

Description: The first assembly of the League of Nations is held in Geneva, Switzerland.
Event title: First assembly of the League of Nations

Description: Nazi Germany bans Jewish children from public schools in the aftermath of Kristallnacht. [11]
Event title: Nazi Germany bans Jewish children from public schools

Description: World War II: The Battle of Guadalcanal ends in a decisive Allied victory.
The Holocaust: German SS leader Heinrich Himmler orders that Gypsies are to be put "on the same level as Jews and placed in concentration camps".
Project Gemini: Gemini 12 completes the program's final mission, when it splashes down safely in the Atlantic Ocean.
Vietnam War: In Washington, D.C., 250,000–500,000 protesters staged a peaceful demonstration against the war, including a symbolic "March Against Death".
Event title: Moratorium protest against the Vietnam War

Description: Intel releases the world's first commercial single-chip microprocessor, the 4004.
The Anglo-Irish Agreement is signed at Hillsborough Castle by British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher and Irish Taoiseach Garret FitzGerald.
In the Soviet Union, the uncrewed Shuttle Buran makes its only space flight.
Event title: Buran makes its first and only space flight

Description: Israeli–Palestinian conflict: An independent State of Palestine is proclaimed by the Palestinian National Council.
A magnitude 7.1 earthquake hits the central Philippine island of Mindoro, killing 78 people, injuring 430 and triggering a tsunami up to 8.5 m (28 ft) high. [18]
Jharkhand officially becomes the 28th state of India, formed from eighteen districts of southern Bihar. [19]
Hu Jintao becomes General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party and a new nine-member Politburo Standing Committee is inaugurated.
Event title: Hu Jintao becomes Chinese Communist Party general secretary

Description: The first day of the 2003 Istanbul bombings, in which two car bombs, targeting two synagogues, explode, kill 25 people and wound 300 more.
Cyclone Sidr hits Bangladesh, killing an estimated 5,000 people and destroying parts of the world's largest mangrove forest, the Sundarbans.
Francisco Pizarro and his men capture Inca Emperor Atahualpa at the Battle of Cajamarca.
King Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden was killed at the Battle of Lützen during the Thirty Years' War. [1]
Event title: Death of Gustavus Adolphus at Lützen

Description: American Revolutionary War: British and Hessian units capture Fort Washington from the Patriots.
French Revolution: Ninety dissident Roman Catholic priests are executed by drowning at Nantes.
Greek War of Independence: The London Protocol entails the creation of an autonomous Greek state under Ottoman suzerainty, encompassing the Morea and the Cyclades.
Historical entity: Great Britain; France; Russia; Ottoman Empire

Description: A Russian court sentences writer Fyodor Dostoyevsky to death for anti-government activities linked to a radical intellectual group; his sentence is later commuted to hard labor.
David Livingstone becomes the first European to see the Victoria Falls in what is now Zambia- Zimbabwe.
Canadian rebel leader of the Métis and "Father of Manitoba" Louis Riel is executed for treason.
English engineer John Ambrose Fleming receives a patent for the thermionic valve (vacuum tube).
Indian Territory and Oklahoma Territory join to form Oklahoma, which is admitted as the 46th U.S. state.
Event title: Admission of Oklahoma to the United States

Description: The Federal Reserve Bank of the United States officially opens.
Event title: Opening of the Federal Reserve Banks

Description: The United States and the Soviet Union establish formal diplomatic relations.
LSD is first synthesized by Albert Hofmann from ergotamine at the Sandoz Laboratories in Basel. [3]
The Holocaust: In occupied Poland, the Nazis close off the Warsaw Ghetto from the outside world.
UNESCO is founded. [5]
Venera program: The Soviet Union launches the Venera 3 space probe toward Venus, which will be the first spacecraft to reach the surface of another planet.
The Arecibo message is broadcast from Puerto Rico.
The Supreme Soviet of the Estonian Soviet Socialist Republic declares that Estonia is "sovereign" but stops short of declaring independence.
In the first open election in more than a decade, voters in Pakistan elect populist candidate Benazir Bhutto to be Prime Minister of Pakistan.
Historical entity: Government of Pakistan; Pakistan Peoples Party

Description: The first cases of the 2002–2004 SARS outbreak are traced to Foshan, Guangdong Province, China. [13]
Elizabethan era begins: Queen Mary I of England dies and is succeeded by her half-sister Elizabeth I.
Articles of Confederation (United States) are submitted to the states for ratification.
Event title: Articles of Confederation submitted for ratification

Description: French Revolutionary Wars: Battle of the Bridge of Arcole: French forces defeat the Austrians in Italy.
Event title: Battle of the Bridge of Arcole

Description: The United States Congress holds its first session in Washington, D.C.
Event title: First U.S. Congress session in Washington

Description: Captain Nathaniel Palmer becomes the first American to see Antarctica. (The Palmer Peninsula is later named after him.)
An earthquake in Valdivia, south-central Chile, causes a tsunami that leads to significant destruction along Japan's coast. [7]
In Egypt, the Suez Canal, linking the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea, is inaugurated.
The Russian Social Democratic Labour Party splits into two groups: The Bolsheviks (Russian for "majority") and Mensheviks (Russian for "minority").
Event title: Russian Social Democratic Labour Party split

Description: Nine Czech students are executed as a response to anti- Nazi demonstrations prompted by the death of Jan Opletal. All Czech universities are shut down and more than 1,200 students sent to concentration camps. Since this event, International Students' Day is celebrated in many countries, especially in the Czech Republic.
American scientists John Bardeen and Walter Houser Brattain observe the basic principles of the transistor, a key element for the electronics revolution of the 20th century.
Lhamo Dondrub is officially named the 14th Dalai Lama.
Cold War: Negotiators from the Soviet Union and the United States meet in Helsinki, Finland to begin SALT I negotiations aimed at limiting the number of strategic weapons on both sides.

Luna programme: The Soviet Union lands Lunokhod 1 on Mare Imbrium (Sea of Rains) on the Moon. This is the first roving remote-controlled robot to land on another world and is released by the orbiting Luna 17 spacecraft.
The Athens Polytechnic uprising against the military regime ends in a bloodshed in the Greek capital.

Cold War: Velvet Revolution begins: In Czechoslovakia, a student demonstration in Prague is quelled by riot police. This sparks an uprising aimed at overthrowing the communist government (it succeeds on December 29).
United States House of Representatives passes a resolution to establish the North American Free Trade Agreement.
Historical entity: United States House of Representatives; NAFTA

Description: In Nigeria, General Sani Abacha ousts the government of Ernest Shonekan in a military coup.
Event title: Sani Abacha seizes power in Nigeria

Description: In Luxor, Egypt, 62 people are killed by six Islamic militants outside the Temple of Hatshepsut, known as Luxor massacre.
Alberto Fujimori is removed from office as president of Peru.
A catastrophic landslide in Log pod Mangartom, Slovenia, kills seven, and causes millions of SIT of damage. It is one of the worst catastrophes in Slovenia in the past 100 years.
The Council of Clermont begins: called by Pope Urban II, it led to the First Crusade to the Holy Land. [3]
Pope Boniface VIII issues the Papal bull Unam sanctam, claiming spiritual supremacy for the papacy. [6]
St Elizabeth's flood: A dike in the Grote Hollandse Waard in the Netherlands breaks, killing about 10,000 people. [7]
Christopher Columbus first sights the island now known as Puerto Rico. [8]
The Battle of Vertières, the last major battle of the Haitian Revolution, is fought, leading to the establishment of the Republic of Haiti, the first black republic in the Western Hemisphere. [13]

King Christian IX of Denmark signs the November constitution that declares Schleswig to be part of Denmark. This is seen by the German Confederation as a violation of the London Protocol and leads to the German–Danish war of 1864.
Susan B. Anthony and 14 other women are arrested for voting illegally in the United States presidential election of 1872.
Event title: Susan B. Anthony arrested for voting

Description: In the "day of two noons", American and Canadian railroad companies institute four standard continental time zones, ending the confusion of thousands of local times. [16]
Event title: North American railroad time zones established

Description: Britain and the United States sign the Hay–Pauncefote Treaty, which nullifies the Clayton–Bulwer Treaty and withdraws British objections to an American-controlled canal in Panama.
The Hay–Bunau-Varilla Treaty is signed by the United States and Panama, giving the United States exclusive rights over the Panama Canal Zone.

In their campaign for women's voting rights, hundreds of suffragettes march to the British Parliament in London. Several are beaten by police, newspaper attention embarrasses the authorities, and the march is dubbed Black Friday. [18]
Latvia declares its independence from Russia.
Release of the animated short Steamboat Willie, the first fully synchronized sound cartoon.

Grand Banks earthquake: Off the south coast of Newfoundland in the Atlantic Ocean, a Richter magnitude 7.2 submarine earthquake, centered on the Grand Banks, breaks 12 submarine transatlantic telegraph cables and triggers a tsunami that destroys many south coast communities in the Burin Peninsula.

World War II: In the first action of the Berlin Air Offensive, four hundred and forty Royal Air Force planes bomb Berlin causing only light damage and killing 131. The RAF loses nine aircraft and 53 air crew. [19]
The Ballantyne's Department Store fire in Christchurch, New Zealand, kills 41; it is the worst fire disaster in the history of New Zealand.
Vietnam War: United States President John F. Kennedy sends 18,000 military advisors to South Vietnam. [20] [21]
Event title: United States expands military advisory mission in South Vietnam

Description: In Jonestown, Guyana, Jim Jones leads his Peoples Temple to a mass murder–suicide that claimed 918 lives in all, 909 of them in Jonestown itself, including over 270 children.
After an 87-day siege, the Croatian city of Vukovar capitulates to the besieging Yugoslav People's Army and allied Serb paramilitary forces.
In South Africa, 21 political parties approve a new constitution, expanding voting rights and ending white minority rule.
Event title: South African parties approve transitional constitution

Description: The Rashidun Caliphate defeats the Sasanian Empire at the Battle of al-Qādisiyyah in Iraq.
The current Saint Peter's Basilica is consecrated in Rome, replacing an earlier basilica on the same site. [2]
The United States and the Kingdom of Great Britain sign Jay's Treaty, which attempts to resolve some of the lingering problems left over from the American Revolutionary War.
Historical entity: United States; Kingdom of Great Britain

Description: American Civil War: U.S. President Abraham Lincoln delivers the Gettysburg Address at the dedication ceremony for the military cemetery at Gettysburg, Pennsylvania.
Serbo-Bulgarian War: Bulgarian victory in the Battle of Slivnitsa solidifies the unification between the Principality of Bulgaria and Eastern Rumelia.
Historical entity: Principality of Bulgaria; Kingdom of Serbia

Description: First Balkan War: The Serbian Army captures Bitola, ending the five-century-long Ottoman rule of Macedonia.
World War II: Battle between HMAS Sydney and HSK Kormoran. The two ships sink each other off the coast of Western Australia, with the loss of 645 Australians and about 77 German seamen.
Event title: Battle between HMAS Sydney and HSK Kormoran

Description: World War II: Battle of Stalingrad: Soviet Union forces under General Georgy Zhukov launch the Operation Uranus counterattacks at Stalingrad, turning the tide of the battle in the USSR's favor.
The Holocaust: Nazis liquidate Janowska concentration camp in Lemberg (Lviv), western Ukraine, murdering at least 6,000 Jews after a failed uprising and mass escape attempt.
Afghanistan, Iceland and Sweden join the United Nations.
Event title: Afghanistan, Iceland and Sweden join the United Nations

Description: Apollo program: Apollo 12 astronauts Pete Conrad and Alan Bean land at Oceanus Procellarum (the "Ocean of Storms") and become the third and fourth humans to walk on the Moon.
TAP Air Portugal Flight 425 crashes in the Madeira Islands, killing 131.
Iran hostage crisis: Iranian leader Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini orders the release of 13 female and black American hostages being held at the US Embassy in Tehran.
Historical entity: Government of Iran; United States government

Description: San Juanico disaster: A series of explosions at the Pemex petroleum storage facility at San Juan Ixhuatepec in Mexico City starts a major fire and kills about 500 people.
Cold War: In Geneva, U.S. President Ronald Reagan and Soviet Union General Secretary Mikhail Gorbachev meet for the first time.
In the United Kingdom, the first National Lottery draw is held. A £1 ticket gave a one-in-14-million chance of correctly guessing the winning six out of 49 numbers.
Event title: First National Lottery draw in the United Kingdom

Description: Clinton–Lewinsky scandal: The United States House of Representatives Judiciary Committee begins impeachment hearings into U.S. President Bill Clinton.
Shenzhou 1: The People's Republic of China launches its first Shenzhou spacecraft.
Historical entity: China National Space Administration; Shenzhou program

Description: The Aviation and Transportation Security Act is enacted by the 107th United States Congress in the immediate aftermath of the September 11, 2001 attacks. The Act created the Transportation Security Administration (TSA). [15]
Event title: Aviation and Transportation Security Act enacted
Historical entity: United States Congress; Transportation Security Administration

Description: The Greek oil tanker Prestige splits in half and sinks off the coast of Galicia, releasing over 76,000 m 3 (20 million US gal) of oil in the largest environmental disaster in Spanish and Portuguese history.
Diocletian is chosen as Roman emperor. [1]
During the An Shi Rebellion, the Tang dynasty, with the help of Huihe tribe, recaptures Luoyang from the rebels.
Zumbi, the last of the leaders of Quilombo dos Palmares in early Brazil, is executed by the forces of Portuguese bandeirante Domingos Jorge Velho.
American Revolutionary War: British forces land at the Palisades and then attack Fort Lee. The Continental Army starts to retreat across New Jersey.
New Jersey becomes the first U.S. state to ratify the Bill of Rights.
Event title: New Jersey ratifies the Bill of Rights

Description: The Second Treaty of Paris is signed, returning the French frontiers to their 1790 extent, imposing large indemnities, and prolonging the occupation by troops of Great Britain, Austria, Prussia, and Russia for several more years. [4]
Modern country: France; United Kingdom; Austria; Prussia; Russia

Description: An 80-ton sperm whale attacks and sinks the Essex (a whaling ship from Nantucket, Massachusetts) 3,200 kilometres (2,000 mi) from the western coast of South America. (Herman Melville's 1851 novel Moby-Dick was in part inspired by this incident.)
Event title: Essex sunk by a sperm whale

Description: Mexican Revolution: Francisco I. Madero issues the Plan de San Luis Potosí, denouncing Mexican President Porfirio Díaz, calling for a revolution to overthrow the government of Mexico, effectively starting the Mexican Revolution.
Event title: Plan of San Luis Potosí issued

Description: World War I: Battle of Cambrai begins: British forces make early progress in an attack on German positions but are later pushed back.
World War II: Hungary becomes a signatory of the Tripartite Pact, officially joining the Axis powers.
World War II: Battle of Tarawa (Operation Galvanic) begins: United States Marines land on Tarawa Atoll in the Gilbert Islands and suffer heavy fire from Japanese shore guns and machine guns.
Historical entity: United States Marine Corps; Imperial Japanese forces

Description: Nuremberg trials: Trials against 24 Nazi war criminals start at the Palace of Justice at Nuremberg.
The Declaration of the Rights of the Child is adopted by the United Nations.
Event title: Declaration of the Rights of the Child adopted

Description: Cuban Missile Crisis ends: In response to the Soviet Union agreeing to remove its missiles from Cuba, U.S. President John F. Kennedy ends the quarantine of the Caribbean nation.
Vietnam War: The Plain Dealer (Cleveland, Ohio) publishes explicit photographs of dead villagers from the My Lai Massacre in Vietnam.
Occupation of Alcatraz: Native American activists seize control of Alcatraz Island until being ousted by the U.S. Government on June 11, 1971.

Egyptian President Anwar Sadat becomes the first Arab leader to officially visit Israel, when he meets Israeli prime minister Menachem Begin and speaks before the Knesset in Jerusalem, seeking a permanent peace settlement.
Historical entity: Government of Egypt; Government of Israel

Description: Grand Mosque seizure: About 200 Sunni Muslims revolt in Saudi Arabia at the site of the Kaaba in Mecca during the pilgrimage and take about 6,000 hostages. The Saudi government receives help from French special forces to put down the uprising.
Microsoft Windows 1.0, the first graphical personal computer operating environment developed by Microsoft, is released. [8]
Velvet Revolution: The number of protesters assembled in Prague, Czechoslovakia, swells from 200,000 the day before to an estimated half-million. [9]
Timur of Samarkand captures and sacks the Georgian capital of Tbilisi, taking King Bagrat V of Georgia captive.
Plymouth Colony settlers sign the Mayflower Compact (November 11, O.S.)
The Danish astronomer Ole Rømer presents the first quantitative measurements of the speed of light.
In Paris, Jean-François Pilâtre de Rozier and François Laurent d'Arlandes make the first untethered hot air balloon flight.
People involved: Jean-François Pilâtre de Rozier; François Laurent d'Arlandes

Description: North Carolina ratifies the United States Constitution and is admitted as the 12th U.S. state. [3]
Event title: North Carolina ratifies the U.S. Constitution

Description: Thomas Edison announces his invention of the phonograph, a machine that can record and play sound.
Port Arthur, China, falls to the Japanese, a decisive victory of the First Sino-Japanese War; Japanese troops are accused of massacring the remaining inhabitants.
Albert Einstein's paper that leads to the mass–energy equivalence formula, E = mc², is published in the journal Annalen der Physik.
World War I: Mines from SM U-73 sink HMHS Britannic, the largest ship lost in the war.
The Parliament (Qualification of Women) Act 1918 is passed, allowing women to stand for Parliament in the UK.
Event title: Women gain eligibility for Parliament in Britain

Description: Irish War of Independence: On " Bloody Sunday" in Dublin, the Irish Republican Army (IRA) assassinated a group of British Intelligence agents, and British forces killed 14 civilians at a Gaelic football match at Croke Park.
The completion of the Alaska Highway (also known as the Alcan Highway) is celebrated (however, the highway is not usable by standard road vehicles until 1943).
The Natural History Museum, London announces that the " Piltdown Man" skull, initially believed to be one of the most important fossilized hominid skulls ever found, is a hoax.
Event title: Piltdown Man exposed as a hoax

Description: The Chinese People's Liberation Army declares a unilateral ceasefire in the Sino-Indian War.
Event title: China declares ceasefire in Sino-Indian War

Description: U.S. President Richard Nixon and Japanese Premier Eisaku Satō agree on the return of Okinawa to Japanese control in 1972. The U.S. retains rights to bases on the island, but these are to be nuclear-free.
Historical entity: Government of Japan; Government of the United States

Description: The first permanent ARPANET link is established between UCLA and SRI.
The Birmingham pub bombings kill 21 people. The Birmingham Six are sentenced to life in prison for the crime but are later exonerated.
A deadly fire breaks out at the MGM Grand Hotel in Paradise, Nevada (now Bally's Las Vegas). Eighty-five people are killed and more than 650 are injured in the worst disaster in Nevada history.
The Dayton Agreement is initialed at the Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, near Dayton, Ohio, ending three and a half years of war in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
Modern country: Bosnia and Herzegovina; Croatia; Serbia; United States

Description: NATO invites Bulgaria, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Romania, Slovakia and Slovenia to become members.
Event title: NATO invites seven states to join
Modern country: Bulgaria; Estonia; Latvia; Lithuania; Romania; Slovakia; Slovenia

Description: Frederick II is crowned Holy Roman Emperor in Rome by Pope Honorius III. [4]
Event title: Frederick II crowned Holy Roman Emperor

Description: Pope Clement V issues the papal bull Pastoralis Praeeminentiae which instructed all Christian monarchs in Europe to arrest all Templars and seize their assets. [5]
Event title: Papal order against the Knights Templar

Description: Spanish navigator Juan Fernández discovers islands now known as the Juan Fernández Islands off Chile. [6]

Royal Navy Lieutenant Robert Maynard attacks and boards the vessels of the British pirate Edward Teach (best known as " Blackbeard") off the coast of North Carolina. The casualties on both sides include Maynard's first officer Mister Hyde and Teach himself. [8]
The Congress of Manastir establishes the Albanian alphabet. [13]
The China Clipper inaugurates the first commercial transpacific air service, connecting Alameda, California with Manila. [15]
Event title: China Clipper inaugurates transpacific air service

Description: World War II: Following the initial Italian invasion, Greek troops counterattack into Italian-occupied Albania and capture Korytsa. [16]
World War II: Battle of Stalingrad: General Friedrich Paulus sends Adolf Hitler a telegram saying that the German 6th Army is surrounded. [17]
Event title: German Sixth Army reported surrounded at Stalingrad

Description: World War II: Cairo Conference: U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill, and Chinese Premier Chiang Kai-shek meet in Cairo, Egypt, to discuss ways to defeat Japan. [18]
Modern country: Egypt; United States; United Kingdom; China
People involved: Franklin D. Roosevelt; Winston Churchill; Chiang Kai-shek

Description: Lebanon gains independence from France, nearly two years after it was first announced by the Free French government. [19]
The Soviet Union launches RDS-37, a 1.6 megaton two stage hydrogen bomb designed by Andrei Sakharov. The bomb was dropped over Semipalatinsk. [21]

U.S. President John F. Kennedy is assassinated and Texas Governor John Connally is seriously wounded by Lee Harvey Oswald, who also kills Dallas Police officer J. D. Tippit after fleeing the scene. [22] Vice President Lyndon B. Johnson is sworn in as the 36th President of the United States afterwards. [23]
People involved: John F. Kennedy; Lee Harvey Oswald; Lyndon B. Johnson

Description: UN Security Council Resolution 242 is adopted, establishing a set of the principles aimed at guiding negotiations for an Arab– Israeli peace settlement. [27]
Juan Carlos is declared King of Spain following the death of Francisco Franco two days earlier. [30]
Event title: Juan Carlos declared King of Spain

Description: NASA launches Space Shuttle Discovery on STS-33, a classified mission for the United States Department of Defense. [32]
Historical entity: NASA; United States Department of Defense

Description: British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher withdraws from the Conservative Party leadership election, confirming the end of her Premiership. [33]
Event title: Margaret Thatcher withdraws from leadership election

Description: The Orange Revolution begins in Ukraine, resulting from the presidential elections. [36]
Conquest of Seville by Christian troops under King Ferdinand III of Castile.
John Milton publishes Areopagitica, a pamphlet decrying censorship. [3]
The start of the 1733 slave insurrection on St. John in what was then the Danish West Indies.
American Civil War: Battle of Chattanooga begins: Union forces led by General Ulysses S. Grant reinforce troops at Chattanooga, Tennessee, and counter-attack Confederate troops. [4]
King William III of the Netherlands dies without a male heir and a special law is passed to allow his daughter Princess Wilhelmina to succeed him.
Event title: Wilhelmina succeeds to the Dutch throne

Description: Mexican Revolution: The last of U.S. forces withdraw from Veracruz, occupied seven months earlier in response to the Tampico Affair.
Warren G. Harding, 29th President of the United States, signs the Willis–Campbell Act into law, prohibiting doctors from prescribing beer or liquor for medicinal purposes. [6]
Edwin Hubble's discovery, that the Andromeda "nebula" is actually another island galaxy far outside our own Milky Way, is first published in The New York Times. [8]
An Anglo-Ethiopian boundary commission in the Ogaden discovers an Italian garrison at Walwal, well within Ethiopian territory. This leads to the Abyssinia Crisis.
Event title: Walwal incident begins the Abyssinia Crisis

Description: World War II: Romania becomes a signatory of the Tripartite Pact, officially joining the Axis powers.
World War II: Tarawa and Makin atolls fall to American forces.
Event title: American capture of Tarawa and Makin
Historical entity: United States Armed Forces; Imperial Japanese forces

Description: French naval bombardment of Hai Phong, Vietnam, kills thousands of civilians.
Representatives of the People's Republic of China attend the United Nations, including the United Nations Security Council, for the first time.
Event title: People's Republic of China takes its UN seat
Historical entity: United Nations; People's Republic of China

Description: Cyclone kills about 1,000 people in eastern Sri Lanka.

Notes: Death toll and injury figures are ranges.
Description: The 6.9 M w Irpinia earthquake shakes southern Italy with a maximum Mercalli intensity of X (Extreme), killing 2,483–4,900, and injuring 7,700–8,934.
The first smartphone, the IBM Simon, is introduced at COMDEX in Las Vegas, Nevada.
The Budapest Convention on Cybercrime is signed in Budapest, Hungary.
Rose Revolution: Georgian president Eduard Shevardnadze resigns following weeks of mass protests over flawed elections.
Event title: Shevardnadze resigns during the Rose Revolution

Description: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf is elected president of Liberia and becomes the first woman to lead an African country.
The Maguindanao massacre occurs in Ampatuan, Philippines; 58 opponents of Andal Ampatuan Jr. are kidnapped and killed. [18]
Genghis Khan defeats the renegade Khwarazmian prince Jalal al-Din at the Battle of the Indus, completing the Mongol conquest of Central Asia. [4]
Abel Tasman becomes the first European to discover the island Van Diemen's Land (later renamed Tasmania).
South Carolina passes the Ordinance of Nullification, declaring that the Tariffs of 1828 and 1832 were null and void in the state, beginning the Nullification Crisis. [7]
British naturalist Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species is published. [8] [9] [10] [11]
Event title: Publication of On the Origin of Species

Description: American Civil War: Battle of Lookout Mountain: Near Chattanooga, Tennessee, Union forces under General Ulysses S. Grant capture Lookout Mountain and begin to break the Confederate siege of the city led by General Braxton Bragg.
In Milwaukee, nine members of the Milwaukee Police Department are killed by a bomb, the most deaths in a single event in U.S. police history until the September 11 attacks in 2001.
World War II: The First Slovak Republic becomes a signatory to the Tripartite Pact, officially joining the Axis powers.
World War II: At the battle of Makin the USS Liscome Bay is torpedoed near Tarawa and sinks, killing 650 men.
World War II: The 73rd Bombardment Wing launches the first attack on Tokyo from the Northern Mariana Islands.
Event title: First Mariana Islands raid on Tokyo

Description: Lee Harvey Oswald, the assassin of President John F. Kennedy, is killed by Jack Ruby on live television. Robert H. Jackson takes a photograph of the shooting that will win the 1964 Pulitzer Prize in Photography.

Joseph-Désiré Mobutu seizes power in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and becomes President; he rules the country (which he renames Zaire in 1971) for over 30 years, until being overthrown by rebels in 1997.
Historical entity: Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo

Description: Apollo program: The Apollo 12 command module splashes down safely in the Pacific Ocean, ending the second crewed mission to land on the Moon.

Donald Johanson and Tom Gray discover the 40% complete Australopithecus afarensis skeleton, nicknamed " Lucy" (after The Beatles song " Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds"), in the Awash Valley of Ethiopia's Afar Depression.
The Çaldıran–Muradiye earthquake in eastern Turkey kills between 4,000 and 5,000 people.

After a week of mass protests against the Communist regime known as the Velvet Revolution, Miloš Jakeš and the entire Politburo of the Czechoslovak Communist Party resign from office. This brings an effective end to Communist rule in Czechoslovakia. [13]
The White Ship sinks in the English Channel, drowning William Adelin, son and heir of Henry I of England. [2]
Baldwin IV of Jerusalem and Raynald of Châtillon defeat Saladin at the Battle of Montgisard. [3]
People involved: Baldwin IV; Raynald of Châtillon; Saladin

Description: A tsunami, caused by an earthquake in the Tyrrhenian Sea, devastates Naples and the Maritime Republic of Amalfi, among other places.
The siege of Granada, the last Moorish stronghold in Spain, ends with the Treaty of Granada.
Historical entity: Emirate of Granada; Crown of Castile

Description: Portuguese conquest of Goa: Portuguese naval forces under the command of Afonso de Albuquerque, and local mercenaries working for privateer Timoji, seize Goa from the Bijapur Sultanate, resulting in 451 years of Portuguese colonial rule.
A deadly earthquake rocks Shemakha in the Caucasus, killing 80,000 people.
French and Indian War: British forces capture Fort Duquesne from French control. Later, Fort Pitt will be built nearby and grow into modern Pittsburgh.
An earthquake hits the Mediterranean destroying Beirut and Damascus and killing 30,000–40,000.
American Revolutionary War: The last British troops leave New York City, three months after the signing of the Treaty of Paris.
Partitions of Poland: Stanisław August Poniatowski, the last king of independent Poland, is forced to abdicate and is exiled to Russia.
A massive undersea earthquake, estimated magnitude between 8.7 and 9.2, rocks Sumatra, producing a massive tsunami all along the Indonesian coast.
A cyclone slams into south-eastern India. An estimated 300,000 deaths resulted from the disaster. [7]

American Civil War: Battle of Missionary Ridge: Union forces led by General Ulysses S. Grant break the Siege of Chattanooga by routing Confederate troops under General Braxton Bragg at Missionary Ridge in Tennessee.
Albert Einstein presents the field equations of general relativity to the Prussian Academy of Sciences.
Vojvodina, formerly Austro-Hungarian crown land, proclaims its secession from Austria-Hungary to join the Kingdom of Serbia.

In Berlin, Germany and Japan sign the Anti-Comintern Pact, agreeing to consult on measures "to safeguard their common interests" in the case of an unprovoked attack by the Soviet Union against either nation.
World War II: Statehood of Bosnia and Herzegovina is re-established at the State Anti-fascist Council for the National Liberation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
Historical entity: State Anti-fascist Council for the National Liberation of Bosnia and Herzegovina

Description: New Zealand ratifies the Statute of Westminster and thus becomes independent of legislative control by the United Kingdom.
Event title: New Zealand adopts the Statute of Westminster
Historical entity: Dominion of New Zealand; British Empire

Description: The Mirabal sisters of the Dominican Republic are assassinated.
People involved: Patria Mirabal; Minerva Mirabal; María Teresa Mirabal

Description: Suriname gains independence from the Netherlands.
Historical entity: Republic of Suriname; Kingdom of the Netherlands

Description: Battle of Caishi: A Song dynasty fleet fights a naval engagement with Jin dynasty ships on the Yangtze river during the Jin–Song Wars.
In the Hawaiian Islands, Captain James Cook becomes the first European to visit Maui.
A national Thanksgiving Day is observed in the United States as proclaimed by President George Washington at the request of Congress.
Official opening of Thomas Telford's Pontcysyllte Aqueduct.
The Battle of Berezina begins during Napoleon's retreat from Russia.
An earthquake as high as magnitude 8.8 rocks the Banda Sea, triggering a tsunami and killing at least 60 in the Dutch East Indies. [2]

United States President Abraham Lincoln proclaims November 26 as a national Thanksgiving Day, to be celebrated annually on the final Thursday of November. Following the Franksgiving controversy from 1939 to 1941, it has been observed on the fourth Thursday in 1942 and subsequent years.
Event title: Thanksgiving proclaimed as a national observance

Description: The Manchester Guardian publishes the 1916 secret Sykes-Picot Agreement between the United Kingdom and France. [4]
The National Hockey League is formed, with the Montreal Canadiens, Montreal Wanderers, Ottawa Senators, Quebec Bulldogs, and Toronto Arenas as its first teams.
Howard Carter and Lord Carnarvon become the first people to enter the tomb of Pharaoh Tutankhamun in over 3,000 years. [6]
The Mongolian People's Republic is officially established after a new constitution, passed by the first State Great Khural, abolishes the monarchy. [7]

World War II: The Hull note is given to the Japanese ambassador, demanding that Japan withdraw from China and French Indochina, in return for which the United States would lift economic sanctions. [8] On the same day, Japan's 1st Air Fleet departs Hitokappu Bay for Hawaii. [9]
Historical entity: United States Department of State; Empire of Japan

Description: World War II: Yugoslav Partisans convene the first meeting of the Anti-Fascist Council for the National Liberation of Yugoslavia at Bihać in northwestern Bosnia.
Event title: Anti-Fascist Council of National Liberation of Yugoslavia convenes

Description: World War II: A German V-2 rocket hits a Woolworth's shop in New Cross, London, killing 168 people.
The Constituent Assembly of India adopts the constitution presented by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar.
Korean War: Communist Chinese troops launch a massive counterattack (Battle of the Ch'ongch'on River and Battle of Chosin Reservoir) against United Nations and South Korean forces.
Event title: Chinese counteroffensive in the Korean War
Historical entity: People's Republic of China; United Nations Command

Description: France launches Astérix, becoming the third nation to put an object in orbit using its own booster.
National Assembly of Azerbaijan abolishes the autonomous status of Nagorno-Karabakh Autonomous Oblast of Azerbaijan and renames several cities with Azeri names.
The Concorde makes its final flight, over Bristol, England. [14]
Mumbai attacks, a series of terrorist attacks killing approximately 175 citizens by 10 members of Lashkar-e-Taiba, a Pakistan based extremist Islamist terrorist organisation.
Pope Urban II declares the First Crusade at the Council of Clermont.
Event title: Council of Clermont declares the First Crusade

Description: An earthquake in northern Morocco devastates the cities of Fes and Meknes. [3]
Adoption of the Constitution of the Kingdom of Poland.
Event title: Constitution of the Kingdom of Poland adopted

Description: James Pratt and John Smith are hanged in London; they are the last two to be executed for sodomy in England.
Event title: Last executions for sodomy in England

Description: American Indian Wars: Battle of Washita River: United States Army Lieutenant Colonel George Armstrong Custer leads an attack on Cheyenne living on reservation land.
At the Swedish–Norwegian Club in Paris, Alfred Nobel signs his last will and testament, setting aside his estate to establish the Nobel Prize after he dies.
Event title: Alfred Nobel signs his final will

Description: The U.S. Army War College is established.
Spain declares a protectorate over the north shore of Morocco.
Event title: Spain declares a protectorate over northern Morocco

Description: In New York City, the first Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is held.
In Romania, the ruling Iron Guard fascist party assassinates over 60 of arrested King Carol II of Romania's aides and other political dissidents.
World War II: At the Battle of Cape Spartivento, the Royal Navy engages the Regia Marina in the Mediterranean Sea.
World War II: At Toulon, the French navy scuttles its ships and submarines to keep them out of Nazi hands.
World War II: RAF Fauld explosion: An explosion at a Royal Air Force ammunition dump in Staffordshire kills seventy people.
CARE (then the Cooperative for American Remittances to Europe) is founded to send CARE Packages of food relief to Europe after World War II.
