The Soviet space program's Mars 2 orbiter releases a descent module. It malfunctions and crashes, but it is the first man-made object to reach the surface of Mars.
Twenty-fifth Amendment: The United States Senate votes 92–3 to confirm Gerald Ford as Vice President of the United States. (On December 6, the House will confirm him 387–35).
Event title: Gerald Ford confirmed as vice president

Description: In San Francisco, city mayor George Moscone and openly gay city supervisor Harvey Milk are assassinated by former supervisor Dan White.
Event title: Assassinations of George Moscone and Harvey Milk
People involved: George Moscone; Harvey Milk; Dan White
Historical entity: City and County of San Francisco

Description: The Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) is founded in the Turkish village of Fis.
Under the Brussels Agreement signed between the governments of the United Kingdom and Spain, the former agrees to enter into discussions with Spain over Gibraltar, including sovereignty.
Historical entity: Governments of the United Kingdom and Spain

Description: A hydrogen atmosphere is discovered on the extrasolar planet Osiris by the Hubble Space Telescope, the first atmosphere detected on an extrasolar planet.
Skanderbeg and his forces liberate Kruja in central Albania and raise the Albanian flag. [3]
After 38 days, an expedition under the command of Ferdinand Magellan completes the first passage through the Strait of Magellan and enters the Pacific Ocean. [5]
Event title: Passage through the Strait of Magellan

Description: At Gresham College, twelve men, including Christopher Wren, Robert Boyle, John Wilkins, and Sir Robert Moray decide to found what is later known as the Royal Society.
Event title: Founding decision of the Royal Society
People involved: Christopher Wren; Robert Boyle; John Wilkins; Robert Moray

Description: The first Treaty of Hopewell is signed, by which the United States acknowledges Cherokee lands in what is now East Tennessee.
The Times of London becomes the first newspaper to be produced on a steam-powered printing press, built by the German team of Koenig & Bauer.
Panama Independence Day: Panama separates from Spain and joins Gran Colombia.
Ka Lā Hui (Hawaiian Independence Day): The Kingdom of Hawaii is officially recognized by the United Kingdom and France as an independent nation.
Women's suffrage in New Zealand concludes with the 1893 New Zealand general election.
The Second Boer War: A British column is engaged by Boer forces at the Battle of Modder River; although the Boers withdraw, the British suffer heavy casualties.
Irish nationalist Arthur Griffith founds Sinn Féin as a political party with the main aim of establishing a dual monarchy in Ireland.
Albania declares its independence from the Ottoman Empire.
Historical entity: Provisional Government of Albania; Ottoman Empire

Description: The Estonian Provincial Assembly declares itself the sovereign power of Estonia.
The Soviet Forces move against Estonia when the 6th Red Rifle Division strikes the border town of Narva, marking the beginning of the Estonian War of Independence. [9]
Event title: Beginning of the Estonian War of Independence

Description: Lady Astor is elected as a Member of the Parliament of the United Kingdom. She is the first woman to sit in the House of Commons. (Countess Markievicz, the first to be elected, refused to sit.)
Event title: Lady Astor enters the House of Commons

Description: Irish War of Independence: Kilmichael Ambush: The Irish Republican Army ambush a convoy of British Auxiliaries and kill seventeen.
In Boston, Massachusetts, a fire in the Cocoanut Grove nightclub kills 492 people.
World War II: Tehran Conference: U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill and Soviet Premier Joseph Stalin meet in Tehran, Iran, to discuss war strategy.
Modern country: Iran; United States; United Kingdom; Russia
People involved: Franklin D. Roosevelt; Winston Churchill; Joseph Stalin

Description: First successful flight of SM-65 Atlas; the first operational intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM), developed by the United States and the first member of the Atlas rocket family. [10]
Mauritania becomes independent of France.
Mariner program: NASA launches the Mariner 4 probe toward Mars.
Antioch suffers its second major earthquake in two years, killing thousands and destroying its remaining edifice. [1]
Following the death of King Chlothar I at Compiègne, his four sons, Charibert I, Guntram, Sigebert I and Chilperic I, divide the Frankish Kingdom. [2]
People involved: Chlothar I; Charibert I; Guntram; Sigebert I; Chilperic I

Description: The papal conclave of 1549–50 begins. [6]
The Battle of Swally takes place, which loosens the Portuguese Empire's hold on India. [7]
Historical entity: Portuguese Empire; English East India Company

Description: Natchez Indians massacre 138 Frenchmen, 35 French women, and 56 children at Fort Rosalie, near the site of modern-day Natchez, Mississippi. [8]
The magnitude 6.6 Irpinia earthquake causes 1,940 deaths in the former Kingdom of Naples, southern Italy. [9]
San Jose, California, is founded as Pueblo de San José de Guadalupe by José Joaquín Moraga. It is the first civilian settlement, or pueblo, in Alta California. [11]
The crew of the British slave ship Zong murders 54 Africans by dumping them into the sea to claim insurance, beginning the Zong massacre. [12]
John VI of Portugal flees Lisbon from advancing Napoleonic forces during the Peninsular War, transferring the Portuguese court to Brazil. [14]
An armed rebellion against Russia's rule in Poland begins. [15]
The treaty, Punctation of Olmütz, is signed in Olomouc. Prussia capitulates to Austria, which will take over the leadership of the German Confederation. [18]
Colorado War: Colorado volunteers led by Colonel John Chivington massacre at least 150 Cheyenne and Arapaho noncombatants at Sand Creek inside Colorado Territory. [20]
Thomas Edison demonstrates his phonograph for the first time. [23]
The Meiji Constitution goes into effect in Japan, and the first Diet convenes. [24]
U.S. Admiral Richard E. Byrd leads the first expedition to fly over the South Pole. [27]
Event title: First flight over the South Pole

Description: The second session of the Anti-Fascist Council for the National Liberation of Yugoslavia (AVNOJ), held to determine the post-war ordering of the country, concludes in Jajce (present-day Bosnia and Herzegovina). [28]
The United Nations General Assembly approve the United Nations Partition Plan for Palestine. [31]
Event title: UN Partition Plan for Palestine approved

Description: Enos, a chimpanzee, is launched into space. The spacecraft orbits the Earth twice and splashes down off the coast of Puerto Rico. [34]
U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson establishes the Warren Commission to investigate the assassination of President John F. Kennedy. [35]
People involved: Lyndon B. Johnson; John F. Kennedy

Description: Atari releases Pong, the first commercially successful video game. [39]
Great Northern War: King Charles XII of Sweden dies during a siege of the fortress of Fredriksten in Norway. [4]
Event title: Death of Charles XII of Sweden

Notes: Later formalized as the 1783 Treaty of Paris.
Description: American Revolutionary War: Treaty of Paris: In Paris, representatives from the United States and Great Britain sign preliminary peace articles (later formalized as the 1783 Treaty of Paris). [5]
Historical entity: United States; Kingdom of Great Britain

Description: The Grand Duchy of Tuscany, under Pietro Leopoldo I, becomes the first modern state to abolish the death penalty (later commemorated as Cities for Life Day). [6]
The Balmis Expedition starts in Spain with the aim of vaccinating millions against smallpox in Spanish America and Philippines. [7]
In New Orleans, Spanish representatives officially transfer the Louisiana Territory to the French First Republic. [8]
Crimean War: Battle of Sinop: The Imperial Russian Navy under Pavel Nakhimov destroys the Ottoman fleet under Osman Pasha at Sinop, a sea port in northern Turkey. [9]

American Civil War: The Confederate Army of Tennessee led by General John Bell Hood suffers heavy losses in an attack on the Union Army of the Ohio under General John Schofield in the Battle of Franklin. [10]
Historical entity: Confederate States of America; United States

Description: The first-ever international football match takes place at Hamilton Crescent, Glasgow, between Scotland and England. [11]
Historical entity: Scotland national football team; England national football team

Description: World War II: The Soviet Red Army crosses the Finnish border in several places, bombing Helsinki and several other Finnish cities, starting the Winter War.
The Holocaust: The SS-Einsatzgruppen round up roughly 25,000 Jews from the Riga Ghetto and kill them in the Rumbula massacre. [14]
World War II: Battle of Tassafaronga; A smaller squadron of Imperial Japanese Navy destroyers led by Raizō Tanaka defeats a U.S. Navy cruiser force under Carleton H. Wright.
Historical entity: Imperial Japanese Navy; United States Navy

Description: Civil War in Mandatory Palestine begins, leading up to the creation of the State of Israel and the 1948 Arab–Israeli War.
Event title: Civil war begins in Mandatory Palestine

Description: Decolonization: Barbados becomes independent from the United Kingdom.
The People's Republic of Southern Yemen gains its independence from the United Kingdom [16]
Iran seizes the Greater and Lesser Tunbs from the Emirates of Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah.
Historical entity: Iran; Emirate of Sharjah; Emirate of Ras Al Khaimah

Notes: The meetings ended inconclusively on December 17.
Description: Cold War: In Geneva, representatives from the United States and the Soviet Union begin to negotiate intermediate-range nuclear weapon reductions in Europe. (The meetings end inconclusively on December 17.)
In Seattle, United States, demonstrations against a World Trade Organization meeting by anti-globalization protesters catch police unprepared and force the cancellation of opening ceremonies.
NASA launches STS-97, the 101st Space Shuttle mission. [18]
Event title: Launch of Space Shuttle mission STS-97
